heroHeadline: NATO 'STILL IN THE DARK' AS PENTAGON CANCELS TOMAHAWK DEPLOYMENT TO GERMANY; NDAA §1249 LEGAL CONSTRAINT IDENTIFIED; HELSINGBORG FMM PREPARATION UNDERWAY
heroSubtitle: Five days after the May 1 withdrawal announcement, NATO remained 'in the dark' on the US drawdown timeline: NATO spokesperson Alison Harte urged allies to 'invest more in defence' while Col. Martin O'Donnell insisted deterrence was unchanged despite SACEUR receiving minimal advance notice. Euronews confirmed on May 5 that the Pentagon had also cancelled the deployment of a Long-Range Fires battalion — armed with Tomahawk cruise missiles and hypersonic weapons — previously promised to Germany by the Biden administration, compounding the blow. A Euronews legal analysis on May 5 identified NDAA §1249 (FY2026) as a statutory constraint prohibiting reduction of US European forces below 76,000 without congressional authorization; the planned withdrawal would bring totals from ~80,000 to ~75,000. On May 6, NATO Deputy Secretary General Radmila Shekerinska met Bosnia-Herzegovina at the North Atlantic Council, underscoring that NATO's institutional operations continue across its broader remit even amid the core alliance crisis. Alliance context: SWORD 26 (15,500 troops) and Amber Shock (Suwałki Gap) exercises remain operational; Rutte met Starmer and Macron at Yerevan EPC (May 4). Upcoming: Helsingborg NATO Foreign Ministers meeting (May 21–22); Ankara Summit (July 7–8).
